text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- King Hussein holds intensive consultations with U.S. President Bill Clinton and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat. King also meets Prince Bandar, the Saudi ambassador to Washington, for talks on means to revitalise peace process.
- Britain backs king's call for probe into all aspects of Jerusalem tunnel. Crown prince Hassan reaffirms Jordan's stand.
- Israel tries to play down Jordan's criticism and rejection of its move.
- Next year's budget is estimated at 1.8 billion dinars, with priority to increasing wages of state employees and executing existing projects. No new jobs and measures to rationalise expenditure.
- Prince Hassan stresses Jordan's role in protecting Moslem holy shrines.
- Jordan plans to offer bids for a tender to build conversion tunnel on Yarmouk river with capacity to hold 50 million cubic metres of water.
- Jordanian initiative on tunnel and holy places provided summit with chance to succeed by halting violence and entering straight into international talks on the issue of Jerusalem.
- Prince Bandar hails king Hussein's efforts in supporting Palestinian rights.
- Prince Hassan says sovereignty over Jerusalem is not issue for bargaining.
- Amman Investment Bank puts forward restructuring plan.
- Tourism minister says Jordan preparing new law for commission to promote tourism.
